jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Sri Lanka has no AI-specific law. Its national AI strategy, 'AI Sri Lanka 2028', was published as a consultation draft in July 2024 and has not been shown as adopted. The Personal Data Protection Act 2022, amended in 2025, gives a right to review decisions based solely on automated processing, with its core provisions applying from 1 January 2027, and the University Grants Commission adopted a national AI policy framework for state universities in 2026. The Ministry of Technology published AI Sri Lanka 2028, a draft national AI strategy, for public consultation in July 2024.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The draft AI strategy is recorded as located only, and an AI white paper and the Online Safety Act are listed as leads. Not yet verified from the official text: the content of the draft AI strategy. A further browser check on 22 October 2026 added records from official sources.

instruments.official_title: Personal Data Protection Act, No. 9 of 2022
instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection Act, No. 9 of 2022
instruments.summary: Sri Lanka's general data protection law governing processing of personal data by public authorities and private controllers and processors, with extraterritorial reach, and establishing the Data Protection Authority. Section 18 gives data subjects a right to request a controller to review a decision based solely on automated processing that has created or is likely to create an irreversible and continuous impact on their rights and freedoms, subject to exceptions (written law, authorisation by the Authority, consent, contract) and safeguards set by Authority rules; refusals can be appealed to the Authority (s.19).
instruments.current_status: Certified 19 March 2022; published as a Supplement to Part II of the Gazette of 25 March 2022. Brought into operation in phases: Part V (Data Protection Authority) from 17 July 2023 (Gazette Extraordinary 2341/59); the 18 March 2025 date for the main provisions (Gazette 2366/08) was replaced after the amendment, and Gazette Extraordinary No. 2498/16 of 22 July 2026 (Order of 13 July 2026) appoints 1 January 2027 for sections 2 and 3, Part I and Part III. Parts II (data subject rights, incl. s.18) and other parts await a commencement order. Amended by Act No. 22 of 2025.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Automated individual decision-making right (s.18) applies to AI-based decisions.
instruments.evidence_reference: Official PDF read with pdftotext on 2026-10-12.

instruments.official_title: Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act, No. 22 of 2025
instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act, No. 22 of 2025
instruments.publisher_name: Data Protection Authority of Sri Lanka
instruments.summary: Amends the Personal Data Protection Act No. 9 of 2022, including the commencement provisions so that sections and parts can be brought into operation in phases by gazetted Order. It widens the automated-decision review right in s.18(1) to decisions affecting rights under the Constitution as well as any written law, and replaces s.19 so data subjects may appeal to the Authority against a refusal to review a decision based solely on automated processing, with the Authority to determine appeals within a prescribed period.
instruments.current_status: Certified 30 October 2025; published as a Supplement to Part II of the Gazette of 31 October 2025. Text hosted on the Data Protection Authority's official site (the DPA's Circular 01/2026 cites the amended Act). Commencement of the amended principal-Act provisions follows Orders under s.1(3) (see the principal Act record).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Strengthens review and appeal rights for solely automated decisions.
instruments.evidence_reference: Official PDF read with pdftotext on 2026-10-12.

instruments.official_title: National Policy Framework for the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the State University System of Sri Lanka
instruments.english_title: National Policy Framework for the Use of Artificial Intelligence in the State University System of Sri Lanka
instruments.summary: UGC framework governing AI adoption across Sri Lanka's state universities, built on nine principles (enablement-first, human-centred, fair and rights-based, transparent and proportionate governance, academic freedom, data stewardship, capacity building, national relevance, sustainability). Its policy statements bar AI as the sole basis for high-stakes decisions about students or staff, give affected individuals rights to explanation, review and redress, and require oversight, documentation and auditability; institutionally adopted AI systems are subject to risk classification and lifecycle governance, while individual use of external generative AI tools is covered by integrity and transparency standards.
instruments.current_status: Dated 2026 on the cover; posted on the UGC policy page. The Ministry of Digital Economy reports it was approved by the UGC on 24 June 2026 with a three-year implementation plan for 2026-2029 and that all state universities are to formulate institutional AI policies under it.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sector-wide AI governance rules for state universities.
instruments.evidence_reference: Official PDF read with pdftotext on 2026-10-12.

instruments.official_title: AI Sri Lanka 2028: Sri Lanka's National Strategy on AI (Draft Strategy for Public Consultation)
instruments.english_title: AI Sri Lanka 2028: Sri Lanka's National Strategy on AI (draft for public consultation)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Technology of Sri Lanka
instruments.current_status: Cover dated July 2024 and marked 'Draft Strategy for Public Consultation'; drafted by the Committee on Formulating a Strategy for AI (CFSAI) appointed in 2023 and first published on the Ministry of Technology's website. The Ministry of Digital Economy later reopened it for public consultation, with feedback to info@mode.gov.lk by 14 March 2025. The consultation has closed and no final strategy has been published.
instruments.summary: A draft national AI strategy aiming at rapid, responsible development and use of AI so that Sri Lanka becomes a digitally empowered country and a regional AI hub. It rests on five enablers (data, skills, infrastructure, research and development, public awareness), two thrusts (responsible public sector transformation and private sector AI uptake) and a safe and trustworthy AI ecosystem. Proposed governance includes a National Centre for AI, a Responsible AI Advisory Council and a monitoring framework, with a Responsible AI Framework first, a review of existing laws and a later AI governance framework.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: A draft national AI strategy aiming at rapid, responsible development and use of AI so that Sri Lanka becomes a digitally empowered country and a regional AI hub.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Sri Lanka's parliament, government printer, digital economy ministry, other ministries and regulators were searched. No AI-specific law or AI bill was found, and there was no material for government AI governance, public-sector use, procurement, cybersecurity, standards, sandboxes, indices, international instruments or older publications. The draft national AI strategy, the 2024 AI white paper, the Online Safety Act text and any central bank AI guidance remain to be checked.

leads.title: Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024
leads.note: Moved to leads at merge: located only (Published as a Supplement to Part II of the Gazette of 2 February 2024 (as indexed; text not read in this review). An Online Safety (Amendment) Bill (2024) and a private member's Online Safety (Repeal) Bill presented 8 May 2025 were found as gazetted bills; their passage was not verified. Official t). Official text could not be read; AI relevance/title unverified. Update 2026-11-07: official Government Printer text read (https://documents.gov.lk/view/acts/2024/2/09-2024_E.pdf). Certified 1 February 2024; Supplement to Part II of the Gazette of 2 February 2024. No mention of 'artificial intelligence' or 'deepfake'. s.52 defines 'bot' and 'coordinated inauthentic behaviour'; s.22 makes it an offence to make or alter bots to communicate offending statements (up to 5 years/Rs 500,000); s.32 lets the Online Safety Commission direct intermediaries to stop bot-controlled or inauthentic accounts. Kept as a lead: no AI provisions, bot misuse only.
